nodes.summary: There is a natural number $d_0$ such that for every natural number $d \ge d_0$ there exists a finite non-empty set $F \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ that forms an aperiodic tiling equation in $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.title: Aperiodic tiling equations in high-dimensional integer lattices

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $d_0$ such that for every natural number $d \ge d_0$ there exists a bounded measurable set $\sigma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of positive Lebesgue measure that forms an aperiodic continuous tiling equation.
nodes.title: Aperiodic continuous tiling equations in high-dimensional Euclidean space

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $\sigma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ forms an aperiodic continuous tiling equation if $\sigma$ continuously tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ with some tiling set $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, and no tiling set $\Lambda$ with which $\sigma$ continuously tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ is periodic.
nodes.title: Aperiodic continuous tiling equation

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group. A set $F \subseteq G$ forms an aperiodic tiling equation if $F$ tiles $G$ with some tiling set $A \subseteq G$, and no tiling set $A \subseteq G$ with which $F$ tiles $G$ is periodic.
nodes.title: Aperiodic tiling equation

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $\sigma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ continuously tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ with tiling set $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ if for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure) there is exactly one $v \in \Lambda$ with $x \in v + \sigma$.
nodes.title: Continuous tiling of Euclidean space

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is periodic if there exist a lattice $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, that is, a discrete additive subgroup that spans $\mathbb{R}^d$ over $\mathbb{R}$, and a finite set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\Lambda = S + L$, so that $\Lambda$ is the union of finitely many cosets of $L$.
nodes.title: Periodic continuous tiling set

nodes.summary: A subset $A$ of an abelian group $G$ is periodic if there exist a subgroup $H$ of $G$ of finite index and a finite set $S \subseteq G$ such that $A = S + H$, that is, $A$ is the union of finitely many cosets of $H$.
nodes.title: Periodic tiling set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $F, A \subseteq G$. Then $F$ tiles $G$ with tiling set $A$ if the map $A \times F \to G$, $(a, f) \mapsto a + f$, is a bijection; equivalently, every element of $G$ lies in $a + F$ for exactly one $a \in A$.
nodes.title: Tiling of an abelian group by translates

nodes.summary: There exist a finite abelian group $G_0$ and a finite non-empty set $F \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2 \times G_0$ that forms an aperiodic tiling equation in the group $\mathbb{Z}^2 \times G_0$.
nodes.title: Greenfeld–Tao counterexample to the periodic tiling conjecture

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
